---
title: Daily Note 2026-03-05
date: 2026-03-05
tags: [daily, rent, stoicism, podcast, cooking]
---

I woke up a bit later than usual today, around 7:45. The apartment was still chilly from the overnight temperature drop so I made a quick cup of coffee and wrapped myself in that old gray blanket while I checked my email. Nothing urgent, just the usual newsletters and a couple of reminders about upcoming bills. The sun was filtering through the blinds in nice stripes across the kitchen table which always puts me in a decent mood even on a weekday.

Around 10 a.m. I finally opened the official letter that had been sitting on the counter for two days. It was the [[rent-increase-notice]] from the property management company. They are raising the rent to $1,480 per month starting June 1. I sat there with my second cup of coffee and ran the numbers in my head. It is not ideal but after comparing it to what similar units are going for in the neighborhood it is still within reason. I spent about twenty minutes weighing the pros and cons: moving would mean packing everything up again, dealing with new landlords, possibly higher moving costs, and I actually like this place. The location is convenient for both work and the weekend farmers market. In the end I decided to renew the lease anyway. I will drop the signed renewal form in the mail tomorrow on my way to the post office. The stability feels worth the extra money for now.

After handling that bit of adulting I treated myself to a long walk around the block. The cherry blossoms are starting to show the first hints of pink. I ran into Mrs. Alvarez from the ground floor unit who was walking her little terrier. We chatted about how the building seems to be getting newer tenants every month. She mentioned that the couple in 3B just had their first baby which explained all the cooing I have been hearing lately.

Back home I spent most of the afternoon listening to a really good [[podcast-episode-stoicism]]. The episode was about applying Stoic principles to everyday frustrations like traffic, difficult coworkers, and unexpected expenses (which felt timely after the rent letter). The host broke down Marcus Aurelius quotes in a way that actually felt practical instead of preachy. I took several pages of notes because I want to revisit them when I am feeling overwhelmed. One line that stuck with me was the idea that we do not control events but we always control our response to them. I am going to try to keep that in mind the next time the printer at work jams for the third time in one morning. I also liked the section on voluntary discomfort. Maybe I should start taking cold showers again like I did last winter.

Later in the evening I decided to cook something more ambitious than my usual weeknight pasta. I made a big pot of chicken curry using that new recipe I found last month. I browned the chicken thighs first which gave everything a nicer depth of flavor. The kitchen smelled incredible while the onions, garlic, ginger, and spices were sautéing. I added coconut milk instead of the usual cream and it turned out silky and rich. I threw in some spinach at the end for a bit of green and served it over basmati rice with a sprinkle of fresh cilantro. It was probably the best curry I have made so far. I even packed leftovers for lunch tomorrow and the day after. Cooking like this always feels like a small act of self care especially after dealing with rent paperwork.

Before bed I spent a little time reviewing my [[weekly-goals]] for March. The rent decision is now locked in so I will need to adjust my budget spreadsheet this weekend. The stoicism podcast gave me some good mental tools to stay calm about it. Overall it was a productive and reflective day. I feel surprisingly at peace with the rent increase and excited to keep experimenting in the kitchen. The apartment may cost a bit more starting in June but at least I will be eating well and trying to keep a level head.

Tomorrow I need to remember to mail that lease renewal and maybe pick up some cardamom pods because I am already thinking about tweaking the curry recipe next time.
